Are you facing problems in team collaboration, storing content, improving productivity, and achieving maximum ROI while using Microsoft SharePoint? If so, such a problem is termed “SharePoint sprawl” as a whole. The issues can be solved by establishing a proper SharePoint governance policy and auditing it on a regular basis.

Let’s learn how you can get the most out of SharePoint lifecycle management by following SharePoint architecture best practices and avoiding mismanagement for your growing business in India.

What Is SharePoint Sprawl?

SharePoint Sprawl is a condition where companies face a situation of a bottleneck in the Microsoft 365 unified collaboration environment, SharePoint lifecycle management,or duplication of sites. Let’s understand it in such a way that you have a team of 100 employees working in your IT department. If any new employee is added, they need to go through several layers of approval to acquire a space in SharePoint.

Such a process quickly declines the productivity and often overlooks SharePoint governance,where your employees rely on timely collaboration. To solve these issues at your evolving organization, you need to eliminate the approval process and manage SharePoint and other Microsoft products like Teams without restriction.

However, ignoring the restriction can compromise your Microsoft 365 environment, as your employees can create multiple SharePoint sites. It may also allow them to use other applications like Outlook and Microsoft Planner, and result in unintentional duplication of groups with the same name, without their knowledge.

So, it is essential for IT departments or key people at your evolving business to determine which site or group a user actually requires access to proper navigation and life cycle management. Let’s learn how you can avoid SharePoint sprawl while mitigating the dispersion across inactive sites, duplicate repositories, or damaged content.

The Impact of Content Mismanagement in SharePoint Governance

Unmanaged content of SharePoint governance while scaling the deployment may lead to operational inefficiencies and a lack of collaboration within the development team. It may push your team towards a shadow IT solution, which may increase the risk of platform adaptation, which may include

  • Provide cluttered and unorganized files with inconsistent naming, which may consume unnecessary space and slow down the compilation process.
  • Hard to set up permission for the specific tasks or individuals, which may lead to security exposure.
  • Create confusion in navigating the right information due to the availability of clustered content.
  • Reduces SharePoint lifecycle management performance due to increased IT support tickets and maintenance burden.
  • Affect the accuracy of your deployment process with duplication or outdated content.

Recommendations to Prevent SharePoint Sprawl

Sprawl in SharePoint happens when it becomes harder to find what you need while expanding our deployment process. Lack of effective SharePoint information architecture can cause increased storage costs and create security or compliance risk. The following features can help you maintain control over your digital workspace and support secure and efficient collaboration.

  • Site Ownership Policy: It is a method to ensure that every site has clear ownership and accountability for SharePoint lifecycle management and governance.
  • AI Insights:Uses of AI with SharePoint architecture best practices help you to identify patterns, spot potential issues, and allow you to take action to keep your content organized and secure while scaling your deployment.
  • Managed Inactive Sites: It allows the use of intelligent agents to address and detect inactive SharePoint sites, reduce cluster content, and optimize your storage.
  • Request Site Attestation: Help you maintain an organized and purposeful Microsoft 365 environment with regular review of prompt site owners and confirm the relevance of sites.

SharePoint Architecture Best Practices for Better Governance While Scaling Your Deployment

If you want smooth governance of your SharePoint, then you need to adopt effective strategies for SharePoint deployment best practices. The tips will help you to establish accurate site creation with an easy approval process and organize your cluster content while scaling your system.

  • Establish a clear SharePoint governance policy with proper naming conventions of sites and content while assigning the roles and responsibilities for site ownership.
  • Adapt a hub and spoke architecture to serve centralized portals for departments or business units while promoting team-specific work, while remaining connected.
  • Use metadata and tagging for efficient content retrieval while removing duplicate or outdated files to improve your content organization and adjust permissions for cost-effective SharePoint governance.
  • Leverage AI tools for content classification and tagging, reduce the chances of errors in your SharePoint lifecycle management,and expand your deployment process smoothly.
  • Limit site creation permission to prevent unnecessary proliferation, with clear guidance to create a new site and terms.
  • Balance governance with team ownership by providing templates, delegate training, and owning site responsibility.
  • Conduct regular audits and clean up the content of the site and libraries to preserve clarity and usability of the space.
  • Educate and empower users on proper content management with the SharePoint architecture best practices to promote a sustainable digital environment.

FAQs

What are the potential reasons behind SharePoint sprawl?

Clustered files, issues in team collaboration, and duplication of content are some of the common issues that impact SharePoint lifecycle management.

How can I take care of SharePoint governance?

You must establish an effective site ownership policy, integrate AI insights, manage inactive sites, and conduct regular audits and reviews to streamline your SharePoint governance.

How can SharePoint architecture best practices streamline my deployment?

Your deployment process can be streamlined with well-planned architecture, automation with intelligent agents, and continuous monitoring and auditing, followed by SharePoint deployment best practices.

How often should I audit my SharePoint content?

You must conduct your audit process weekly, monthly, or biannually based on your data to clean up outdated files, permissions, and unused sites.
